turns.prompt: when I end a meeting, the recap leaves out any task that has a person on it but no deadline. like if they say 'Priya will send the contract' with no date it just isnt in the action items. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
Fixed. The model was actually returning those tasks. A filter in `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts:235` threw them away after the fact: it only kept action items that contained a digit or a date word like "by", "due", "tomorrow" or "friday". "Priya will send the contract" has none of those, so it was silently dropped.

What I changed in `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`:
- **Removed that filter.** Every action item the model returns now stays in the recap. If the model sends back something that isn't a list, it falls back to an empty list instead.
- **Updated the summary prompt** so it tells the model to keep tasks that have an owner but no due date, to put the owner first (e.g. "Priya: Send the contract"), and never to make up a date. This matches the rule already in `electron/llm/prompts.ts`.

I haven't tested it. `node_modules` doesn't seem to be installed, so the type check didn't run, and I haven't ended a real meeting to check the recap. The change is small, but end one quick test meeting with an undated task to confirm it shows up.

One thing still works the old way: if a meeting mode with custom note sections is active, that path never used this filter. It also doesn't have a separate action-items list, so how undated tasks show up there depends on that mode's sections.

I found the real cause this time. My first fix only covered the Gemini/default prompt. If you have a Groq key, the recap goes through a separate Groq prompt, and that one never said to keep undated tasks. Its only example was "Bob: Draft invite copy by Wednesday", so the model learned that every action item needs a date and skipped "Priya will send the contract."

What I changed this round:
- **Groq prompt** (`electron/llm/prompts.ts`, around line 375): it now says to include every task that has an owner even without a due date, never to make up a date, and gives "Priya: Send the contract (no date given)" as an example.
- **Small local model prompts** (`electron/llm/tinyPrompts.ts`): I added the same rule to the summary prompt. I also changed the team-meeting live notes format, which used "📋 Who to What by When", so it writes "no date given" instead of dropping the item.
- **Missing overview** (`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`): the Groq prompt returns the meeting overview under the name "summary", but the screen looks for "overview", so the overview was coming up blank on Groq. It now uses "summary" when "overview" is missing.

The earlier fix still stands: the step that deleted undated items after the model answered is gone, and I checked that nothing else removes them before the meeting is saved.

I haven't tested any of this. There's no `node_modules` or compiled build in this folder, so I couldn't type-check it or run the app. The app runs from compiled files in `dist-electron`, not from the source, so these edits won't show up until you rebuild. If you were trying it without a rebuild, that alone would explain why the first fix seemed to do nothing. Run `npm run electron:dev` (or `npm start`), end a short meeting where someone says something like "Priya will send the contract," and check that it appears in the action items.

If it still doesn't show up after a rebuild, tell me which AI provider you use (Groq, Gemini, a custom one or the Natively API) and whether a meeting mode was on. A mode with custom note sections skips the action items list entirely.

I found two more causes this round, and either one could still drop "Priya will send the contract."

- **The recap only saw the first 10,000 characters of the meeting**, roughly the first 10 minutes. Tasks usually get handed out at the end, so in any longer meeting the model never saw them. It now gets the opening plus the last ~32,000 characters (`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts:207`).
- **Team Meet mode only asked for your own tasks.** If you're using it, the instruction for its Action Items section was "All action items that were said I would do after the meeting." So Priya's task was left out by design. I changed it to every task assigned to anyone, owner first, including ones with no due date (`electron/services/ModesManager.ts`).

The Team Meet change only applies to newly created modes. Your existing Team Meet mode probably saved the old wording when you created it. To cover that, I added a rule that every recap prompt uses: include every task with a named owner, even with no date, and never make up a date. That rule applies whether or not a mode is on.

I still haven't run any of this. There's no `node_modules` or compiled build in this folder, so I can't type-check, build or test it. You have to rebuild before any of these edits take effect: run `npm start` or `npm run electron:dev`. Restarting an old build won't pick them up.

If it still fails after a rebuild, send me two things from the terminal output after you end a meeting:
- The line starting `[MeetingPersistence] Raw LLM summary response`, which shows whether the model is dropping the task or something later is.
- The line starting `[MeetingPersistence] Active mode:` (or "No active mode"), which shows which prompt was used.

With those I can find the exact spot instead of guessing.
